These models work the same in video mode and in image mode: video generates one image per scene with the same model.

Retouch models change a picture you give them from an instruction ("put a red cap on him"). There are two engines: Fast (FLUX.1 Kontext, about 40 s, non-commercial licence) and Precise (Qwen-Image-Edit, about 2 min, commercial use allowed). Each is several files installed together from the catalog; they are not downloaded one by one.
LoRAs tweak the style or subject of an image model.
Video models animate an image (or start from text) to create clips with real motion. Each model is several files — the model, a text encoder and a VAE — installed together.

Music models create full songs from a style and, if you want, your lyrics. Each package is four files — language model, text encoder, synthesis model and VAE — installed together; the last three are shared between packages. The engine is also required (bash scripts/build-acestep.sh). Adapters (LoRA) change the sound of all songs without changing the model: they are installed here and chosen in the studio; an adapter is a file or a folder with two files.
Voices are only used in video mode (narration). Image mode does not need them.
